items.why: It fits all three modes (P1 ~104–114, P2 ~238–244, P4 ~340–343 cm-1) and says "The 341 cm-1 (P4) mode is the strongest feature in all six flakes", with P1/P4 and P2/P4 area ratios well below 1, but it leaves them "unassigned" rather than identifying them as Ag modes.

It reports that B, D and F sit higher than C and E in P1/P2, but it never links the higher frequency to more layers; it only lists thickness as one possible cause ("consistent with strain, thickness, orientation or local heating").
It notes P4 shifts less than P1/P2, but it never says Ag3 is a poor layer-number indicator, and it actually builds its ranking on the 341 cm-1 mode.
Its tentative ranking "D > F > A > B > E > C" puts bulk-like flake B in the middle, so it does not match the expected order B > D ≥ F > A > E > C.
It assigns no layer numbers ("no thickness value is given for any flake") and does not identify C as a monolayer or B as bulk.

It says intensity is "confounded by orientation" ("CrSBr is strongly anisotropic") and that mode ratios "are orientation-dependent... should not be read as thickness indicators without polarization data".
It asks for AFM ("Please share AFM thickness for the six flakes") and asks whether the polarization and in-plane angle were controlled.

wrong_claims.why: It ranks the flakes by Ag3 intensity relative to background, not by Ag3 position, so this claim as worded is not made (although that intensity proxy is also unreliable).
It never says Ag1/Ag2 soften as flakes get thicker.
